question: What constitutes the wholesale and retail trade sector in Uganda and how are general traders categorized for taxes?
answer: Wholesale trade involves purchasing merchandise in commercial quantities from manufacturers or primary distributors and reselling to retailers (or directly to institutional buyers); retail trade involves purchasing from wholesalers and selling finished consumer goods in smaller units directly to final consumers. For tax purposes, URA categorizes traders into three operational groups: 1) Small Business (Presumptive) Taxpayers — resident traders with gross turnover between UGX 10,000,000 and UGX 150,000,000 per year (averaging at least UGX 34,700 daily); 2) VAT-Registered Traders — entities whose taxable supplies exceed UGX 37.5 million in 3 consecutive months or UGX 150 million in 12 months (or UGX 75M quarterly / UGX 300M annually under revised schedules), or who register voluntarily; 3) Standard Corporate / Large Commercial Traders — taxed under 30% Corporation Tax on net business profits.

question: How does the presumptive tax regime apply to small wholesale and retail traders in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines published by Okao Brian (August 30, 2023 - 12:24 pm) at https://ura.go.ug/en/small-business/: 1) Gross turnover under UGX 10,000,000 pays Nil tax; 2) Gross turnover between UGX 10M and UGX 150M pays simplified presumptive tax based on gross sales, serving as a final tax without separate business deductions; 3) Rates with records: UGX 10M–30M: 0.4% on excess over 10M; UGX 30M–50M: UGX 80,000 + 0.5% on excess over 30M; UGX 50M–80M: UGX 180,000 + 0.6% on excess over 50M; UGX 80M–150M: UGX 360,000 + 0.7% on excess over 80M; 4) Fixed lump-sum rates without records apply for non-bookkeepers; 5) Payment of small business tax doubles as filing your income tax return.

question: What are the VAT thresholds, input-output offset rules, and refund criteria for wholesale and retail traders?
answer: Under URA VAT guidelines (Vol. 2 Issue 4 FY 2023-24) at https://ura.go.ug/en/vat-registered-category/: 1) Standard-rated supplies attract 18% VAT, zero-rated supplies attract 0% VAT, and exempt supplies (unprocessed foodstuffs, passenger transport, financial services) attract no VAT; 2) Compulsory registration applies if taxable sales exceed the statutory threshold; voluntary registration is open to businesses below the threshold if they maintain a fixed business premises, proper records, and fit-and-proper status; 3) Mechanism: Trader charges 18% Output VAT on sales and claims credit for 18% Input VAT incurred on business purchases/imports; the difference is payable to URA (or claimable if input exceeds output); 4) VAT Refund: Traders in an excess input position exceeding UGX 5,000,000 can apply for a cash refund from URA, or roll forward the credit to offset future VAT liabilities.

question: How do EFRIS e-invoicing and Digital Tax Stamps (DTS) apply to wholesale and retail traders?
answer: Under URA guidelines and the Wholesale & Retail Taxation Guide: 1) EFRIS: All VAT-registered traders must issue electronic fiscal receipts and invoices through EFRIS at the point of sale; non-VAT registered traders can voluntarily issue e-receipts; buyers can only claim VAT input tax credit if supported by valid EFRIS fiscal invoices bearing a 20-digit Fiscal Document Number (FDN); 2) EFRIS auto-populates monthly VAT returns, simplifying monthly filing due by the 15th; 3) Digital Tax Stamps (DTS): Wholesalers and retailers distributing gazetted excisable goods (beers, spirits, wines, bottled mineral water, carbonated soft drinks, tobacco products, cement, and sugar) must ensure every product unit bears an activated physical digital tax stamp or digital code; dealing in unstamped gazetted goods attracts seizure, 100% penal tax, and criminal prosecution.

question: What tax incentives and capital allowances apply to wholesale and retail traders in Uganda?
answer: Under the URA Wholesale & Retail Sector Taxation Guide (FY 2022-23): 1) 10-Year Income Tax Holiday: Exporters of finished consumer and capital goods who export at least 80% of their production enjoy a 10-year income tax exemption; 2) Initial Capital Allowance: 50% accelerated capital deduction on qualifying plant & machinery, and 20% on industrial buildings situated outside Kampala (50 km radius); straight-line 5% annual depreciation on industrial buildings for 20 years; 3) Research & Training Deductions: 100% deduction of scientific research expenditures and 100% deduction of staff training expenses (up to 5 years); 4) PWD Employment: 2% deduction from income tax payable for employers with at least 5% full-time employees with disabilities; 5) 6% WHT Exemption: Compliant taxpayers receive a 12-month renewable WHT exemption certificate; 6) Nil Stamp Duty on credit collateral: 0% stamp duty on security bonds and mortgage deeds executed to secure commercial loans.

question: What customs taxes and import duties apply to general goods imported by wholesale and retail traders?
answer: When importing goods into Uganda, wholesale and retail traders pay: 1) Customs Import Duty: Calculated on CIF value (Cost + Insurance + Freight) based on the EAC Common External Tariff (CET 4-band structure: 0% raw materials, 10% intermediate goods, 25% finished consumer goods, 35% sensitive items); 2) Value Added Tax (VAT): 18% charged on (Customs Value + Import Duty + Excisable Duty if applicable); 3) Withholding Tax (WHT): 6% on customs value of imported goods (waived for compliant traders with WHT exemption); 4) Infrastructure Levy: 1.5% of Customs Value on dutiable non-EAC imports; 5) Environmental Levy: Charged on specified used goods and motor vehicles.

question: Where can I download the official URA guides for the wholesale and retail sector?
answer: Official publications are available on the URA portal: 1) 'A Guide to Taxation of the Wholesale and Retail Sector' (FY 2022-23, 36 pages) downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2024/06/Aguide-To-Taxation-Of-The-Wholesale-And-Retail-Sector22-23-1.pdf, published under Tax Education by Esther Watsemwa on June 24, 2024 - 2:54 pm (https://ura.go.ug/en/overview-of-wholesale-and-retail/); 2) 'Value Added Tax (VAT)' booklet (Vol. 2 Issue 4 FY 2023-24, 5 pages) downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2025/01/VALUE-ADDED-TAX-VAT-Vol-2-Issue-4-FY-2023-24.pdf, authored by Okao Brian on August 30, 2023 - 12:33 pm (https://ura.go.ug/en/vat-registered-category/); 3) 'Small Business' guide authored by Okao Brian on August 30, 2023 - 12:24 pm (https://ura.go.ug/en/small-business/).
